anomalies.observed: In the ATO driver, T5’s gate net G_ATO is connected to T4’s collector and pulled down to GND through R12 (10 kΩ). The ATO_VALVE signal drives T4’s base, but no connection sources the T5 gate to a voltage that turns the N-channel AO3400A on.
anomalies.expected: The ATO low-side switch needs a gate-drive path that can raise T5’s gate to turn it on. The main-pump driver provides a +3V3 pull-up at the corresponding gate node (R5); the ATO driver should likewise have an effective gate-high drive rather than only a pull-down.

evidence.quote: "ATO_VALVE"; "T4 BT3904"; "R12 10k"; "T5 AO3400A" (sheet 1, lower-left, Main Pump & Valve Drivers)
"+3V3"; "R5 10k" (sheet 1, lower-left, Main Pump & Valve Drivers; main-pump gate-bias network)
“T3 — AON6407 (8-DFN N-MOSFET) | ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch” and “gate driven through R10 (100 Ω), pre-driven via T4 (BT3904).” (Component Table)

anomalies.impact: The ATO MOSFET is not driven on by the shown circuit, so the solenoid valve is likely to remain off and automatic top-off will not operate.

parsed.summary: The ATO driver’s MOSFET gate is pulled to ground and has no shown gate-high drive. As drawn, T5 is unlikely to switch on, preventing the ATO valve from opening.
